credit_system.credit_hour: 1 credit equals about 45 hours of work per semester; a 3-credit course is about 135 hours, or roughly nine hours per week for about 15 weeks.
credit_system.grading: Letter grades A to F; GPA on a 4.0 scale (Montana University System scale).
credit_system.math_placement: Students take the MSU Math Placement; Business majors with Math Placement level 400+ are exempt from M 121Q College Algebra.

dataset_note: Facts copied from official MSU pages, checked on 2026-10-17. A null field means the data was not found in the source.

majors.name: Computer Science, B.S. (Professional Option)
majors.accreditation: Computing Accreditation Commission of ABET (bachelor's program)
majors.description: Four-year degree with depth in computer science and related technical areas. Other paths in the same school: Interdisciplinary Option (pairs CS with a minor such as Entrepreneurship or Japanese Studies), a B.A. in Computer Science with fewer math and science courses, and an accelerated B.S./M.S. in five years.
majors.career_outcomes: The catalog cites U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics projections that computing occupations will grow much faster than average, with about 356,700 openings per year. Specific job titles are not listed in the catalog.
majors.first_thing_to_check: Try CSCI 127 (Joy and Beauty of Data) in the first semester to see if programming fits you.
majors.labs_note: No labs or faculty research areas in the beta dataset. School director listed on the department site: John Paxton.

majors.name: Data Science, B.S.
majors.description: Integrates computing, statistics, mathematics, business and English.
majors.first_thing_to_check: Read the Data Science B.S. page in the MSU catalog and compare it with the Computer Science B.S.
majors.labs_note: Thin data in the beta: course list and career outcomes not collected yet.

majors.name: Mechanical Engineering, B.S.
majors.description: Builds strength in fundamentals, applications, design, communication and professional responsibility. Covers math, physics, chemistry, thermodynamics, heat transfer, fluid mechanics and materials science. Ends with a team capstone that builds a working prototype. At least 42 credits must be 300-level or above.
majors.career_outcomes: Process industries (pulp and paper, steel, aluminum, food, petroleum, chemicals); manufacturing (highway vehicles, instruments, airplanes, rockets and engines, toys, agricultural machinery); power plants (steam, nuclear, hydroelectric); federal laboratories; consulting (HVAC design, forensic engineering); manufacturing management.
majors.first_thing_to_check: Take EMEC 100 (Introduction to Mechanical Engineering) in the first year.
majors.labs_note: No labs or faculty in the beta dataset. Department phone listed on its site: (406) 994-2203.

majors.name: Business, B.S. (Management Option)
majors.department: Jake Jabs College of Business & Entrepreneurship
majors.college: Jake Jabs College of Business & Entrepreneurship
majors.description: Focuses on leadership, communication, team management, strategic thinking, problem solving and ethical decision making.
majors.math_note: Requires M 121Q College Algebra (students with MSU Math Placement level 400+ are exempt) and STAT 216Q.
majors.career_outcomes: Management and supervision; sales and entrepreneurship; consulting and operations; product development and analytics; international business and project management; human resources and supply chain; public administration. Industries include technology, aerospace, healthcare, retail, government, non-profit and hospitality.
majors.first_thing_to_check: Read the Management option page and look at BMGT 335 (Management and Organization).
majors.labs_note: No faculty data in the beta dataset.

majors.name: Business, B.S. (Finance Option)
majors.department: Jake Jabs College of Business & Entrepreneurship
majors.college: Jake Jabs College of Business & Entrepreneurship
majors.description: Covers how organizations raise and manage money, how investment portfolios balance return and risk, and how financial institutions and markets allocate capital.
majors.math_note: Requires M 121Q College Algebra (students with MSU Math Placement level 400+ are exempt) and STAT 216Q.
majors.career_outcomes: Credit, financial and securities analysis; bank examination; lending; treasury and comptroller functions; portfolio management; financial planning; insurance underwriting.
majors.first_thing_to_check: Look at ECNS 204IS (Microeconomics) and ACTG 201 as early tests of interest.
majors.labs_note: No faculty data in the beta dataset.
